title: Rows of chickens
_map: Lesson map: Rows of chickens (Y1–2) + Turn the farm (Y2). Big idea: multiplication is equal rows (an array); 3 × 4 is the same array turned round.
_stepChain: a row (from stack-64) → equal rows → the same 12 chickens can make different equal rows → some numbers of rows leave chickens over → the shape of equal rows is called an array → 3 rows of 4 and 4 rows of 3 are the same array turned round

talk.ask: How many different ways did you find to put 12 chickens in equal rows?
talk.goodAnswer: 1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4, 4 × 3, 6 × 2, 12 × 1. Some numbers of rows, like 5, leave chickens over.

talk.ask: Is 3 rows of 4 the same as 4 rows of 3? How do you know?
talk.goodAnswer: yes, both are 12. It's the same array turned round: the rows become the columns.

handsOn: Get 12 Lego bricks, or 12 spoons. Lay them in equal rows in as many ways as you can. Then turn your array round and count again.

narration.text: The farm has 12 chickens, and they want to line up for breakfast. They like standing in rows, and every row must have the same number of chickens.
How many rows should they make? Choose a number of rows, then tap the hammer. See what happens. Try lots of different numbers.
Look at all the ways you found. When things stand in equal rows, the shape they make is called an array. Some numbers of rows left chickens over. Those chickens couldn't make a full row.
Here's a puzzle. 3 rows of 4 chickens. Now turn the whole farm round, so the rows go the other way. It's 4 rows of 3.

question.prompt: Which has more chickens? Make your best guess.
question.reveal: They're the same! Turning the array round doesn't add or take away any chickens. 3 times 4 and 4 times 3 are both 12.

rule.ask: Can you say why 3 rows of 4 is the same as 4 rows of 3? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye to check.
rule.spoken: Equal rows make an array. And turning an array round doesn't change how many: 3 times 4 equals 4 times 3.

bonus.prompt: Bonus challenge: how many ways can 24 chickens make equal rows? Make a guess.
bonus.reveal: There are 8 ways: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24 rows. 24 can make more arrays than 12 can.
